blocking.where: scope_b.sh l.73 (register regex), l.83-86 (E glob translation); PROTOCOL-B §1 leading (^|/), §3 norm-register paths
blocking.summary: The register regex needs the token at the start of a path segment, so engineering/architecture/adr/ADR-AIP-LOG-Platform-Rulings.md matches no channel. After the BLK-1 split, K-NORMREG is the only norm source for N_c.
blocking.consequence: No other register path: K-NORMREG gets NOT_EVIDENCED_AT_TIPS (a false existence negative), K-STATUS and K-DEPLOY get IND[no_norm_source_distinct_from_candidate] (a false label), and the positive cannot be reached. Some other register path exists: the norm-maker's authors are missing from N_c, overlap_norm is undercounted, and a positive that the qualifier does not cover becomes possible.
blocking.fix: Allow an infix leading boundary for the register tokens, e.g. (^|[/._-]), or add an explicit ADR/rulings rule. Widen the E exclusion globs the same way. Alternatively, declare that infix names are out of scope and qualify the no_norm_source label.

nonblocking.summary: GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS / GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS / GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS / GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS and GIT_TRACE* / GIT_TRACE2* are not unset. An inherited GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 disables pathspec magic and silently empties E and W. Trace vars can write path pathspecs outside OUT. Existed before r2.

The register and status vocabularies catch data files inside the code roots (e.g. config/decisions.yml -> SELF_ATTESTED 'by definition'; lang/*/status.json -> K-STATUS with developer writers). Not forced, but imprecise. Declare in §6.
